provider: CUHK Department of Computer Science and Engineering 2026 BCSE curriculum
note: The official 49-page 2026 BCSE academic counselling deck (4,197,704 bytes; SHA-256 9057a87c816ba15d0390223668961bd7c788e221711e989c33274bbcb9600fec) was text-extracted and curriculum/allocation pages 10-29 were rendered and visually reviewed. It confirms that BCSEN is a common-entry Programme whose students are allocated after Year 1 to Computer Engineering (CENG) or Computer Science (CSCI), each with a 75-unit Major requirement. The one-page CENG and CSCI flowcharts, both last updated 2026-08-01, were visually reviewed in full; their SHA-256 values are 0b5acfc3087a4121522a62d50267374fda5ac44016ff089fb7e56dfbe81ef070 and 8eab98d3c2639d1e4c4e4dcf2dbb83877a3002ff1faf9e7d2d962e94e6210ea3. This supplement expands every explicitly printed standard/ESTR alternative as a distinct Programme-local course and uses the current official CSE Course List to cross-check titles and units. ENGG1111 is retained as the current zero-unit AI Literacy Workshop because the counselling deck lists it among the common-entry registration requirements. ENGG1040 and ENGG1004 are excluded because the flowcharts make them conditional placement-test bridge courses rather than part of the 75-unit Major requirement. The CSCI flowchart prints ENGG1100/ESTR1002, while the counselling common-year slide, allocation-eligibility slide and current CSE Course List all identify the course as ENGG1110/ESTR1002; this supplement uses ENGG1110 and does not invent an ENGG1100 title. Foundation Science has no fixed code, and neither the two CENG Streams nor the six CSCI Streams publish a closed course-code pool in these materials. Stream/ELITE/double-degree choices, slash alternatives, the uncoded Foundation Science choice and placement-test exceptions are therefore not closed by the local rule engine. Both Major lists remain browse-only with totalCreditRequired=0 and no graduation completion percentage.
